description.narrative: ltpgtObjective: 800 vulnerable households in the targeted areas of Khersonska, Chernhivska, and Sumska oblasts will receive emergency shelter and NFI assistance mitigating the impacts of winter weather for internally displaced, returnees, and non-displaced people while minimizing environmental impact via the provision of solid fuel for Winter Energy (SN 108) to 800 households and Insulation of Substandard Houses (SN 105) to 200 households. lt/pgtltpgtContext: Ongoing hostilities and shelling, destruction of infrastructure and social facilities, power outages, inflation, job lost and other full-scale war effects make the winter period difficult and even life-threatening for vulnerable categories of the population. Internally displaced persons (IDPs), non-displaced persons in conflict-affected areas, returnees, and host communities will be particularly impacted, especially persons with compounding vulnerabilities such as people with disabilities, elderly people, women and children, and others. The lack of adequate shelter combined with heating issues threatens to cause further loss of life and displacement among these groups of affected people.ltbrgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtFocusing on Shelter/NFI Cluster Winter Objectives 2 and 3 and based on experience of winterization response 2023-2024, to effectively address the specific challenges posed by winter conditions in Ukraine, GER3 and its sub-implementing partner will provide insulation of 200 sub-standard houses and distribution of winter energy for 800 households in border and frontline oblasts (Sumska, Chernihivska, Khersonska) where GER3 and District #1 have operational presence and previously implemented shelter and winterization activities. ltbrgtGER3 and its partner also have strong existing relationships with local governments and civil society partners in the areas of implementation. The needs analysis, targeting, and implementation of our proposed response is also informed by data and information gathered during post-distribution monitoring of 2023-2024 winterization activities. ltbrgtThis presence has provided GER3 with a high level of contextual knowledge and understanding of humanitarian needs, as well as an appreciation of the challenges and mitigating actions required to operate safely and effectively in the region. GER3 and its partner also have strong existing relationships with local governments and civil society partners in the areas of implementation. lt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtGER3 – Sumska oblast (Krolevetska hromada) – 50 insulated HH and 200 HH supported with solid fuel.ltbrgtGER3 – Chernihivkda oblast (Bakhmatska and Kulykivska hromadas) – 50 insulated HH and 200 supported with solid fuel.ltbrgtGER3 – Khersonska oblast (Velykooleksandrivska hromada) – 50 insulated HH and 200 HH supported with solid fuel.ltbrgtDistrict #1 – Khersonska oblast (Kalynivska hromada) – 50 insulated HH and 200 HH supported with solid fuel. ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtAs a result, 2400 people will be provided with safe and dignified living conditions during harsh winter period. This project will complement ongoing GER3 light/medium repair projects in the targeted areas and planned winterization activities.ltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtltbrgtlt/pgtltpgtGER3 has the financial and team capacity to begin project works prior to receipt of the first tranche of funding, if necessary. lt/pgt
